author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
One of the best--and worst--things about PC gaming is the support for mods, allowing users to customize their games to an absurd degree. Installing a mod isn't always straightforward, and the more it remixes a game, the greater the chance of that title crashing, burning, and frustrating the user on the other end. Nexus Mods, one of the largest sites in the modding community, is aiming to fix that issue with a long-term plan to make mods easier to access and use.

Following a change in leadership last year that saw Victor "Foledinho" Folmann take over, the current boss of the site has penned an open letter describing plans to change the very nature of how mods are presented, shared, and accessed on the longrunning site.
title: Nexus Mods Wants To Replace Modding Frustration With One-Click Simplicity

author: S.E. Doster
description:
The Simpsons are returning to Fortnite with new and improved content on July 30, but this time Springfield will be featured as a Reload map. Epic Games has confirmed some of the new and returning content, including the Simpson's version of John Wick and a new Sprite.

Last year's Fortnite x The Simpsons crossover event was a massive success for Epic Games, delivering an explorable, cel-shaded version of Springfield. The map's return in Fortnite Reload will also bring back several fan-favorite loot items, including the Mr. Blasty gun, Krusty Burger, Blinky Fish, Super Squishee, and the Cartoon Chainsaw.

With this being the Reload version of Springfield, the map will also feature re-lootable chests and the ability to reboot as solo players. The
title: The Simpsons Return To Fortnite This Week With John Wick

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Mystery games have started to become popular again over the last couple of years, but one studio is aiming to put a new spin on the genre with The Eventide. Billed as a supernatural mystery that follows a team of paranormal investigators through a stylized Canadian neon-noir cityscape, players will have to monitor and study strange cases that have escaped the public eye. The twist here? A "perspective-driven" approach to solving strange cases straight out of The X-Files, as you'll have to use human resources to help crack these mysteries.

The debut game from Studio Reset--a developer comprised of people who previously worked on Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and The Long Dark--the Parallax Deduction system drives players to assign the right investigators to each case. Depending on who you task to work the investigation, the outcome might vary wildly. Each agent brings their own background, beliefs, expertise, and way of
title: This X-Files-Inspired Detective Game Wants You To Solve Mysteries From Every Angle

title: Double Fine Cuts 25% Of Staff After Separating From Microsoft

The new Spider-Man movie sees its star, Tom Holland, once again do whatever a spider can, which apparently includes using finishing moves from the recent Spider-Man games. author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
Silent Hill: Townfall makes some big changes from the usual Silent Hill experience that fans have come to expect, not only with its Scottish setting, but also with its first-person perspective. While this gameplay style is unusual for Silent Hill (we still remember you, PT), it turns out there was really no debate about whether it was right for Townfall.

Speaking at a media roundtable event that GameSpot attended, director Jon McKellan said that from the very start, Silent Hill: Townfall was planned as a first-person game.

"It was first-person from day one
title: Here’s Why Silent Hill: Townfall Is A First-Person Game

author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
Over the past few years, we've seen a major revival of the Silent Hill franchise, with 2024's Silent Hill 2 remake offering a spectacular reimagining of one of the series' most beloved entries while titles like Silent Hill f and Townfall propel the series forward and seek to redefine what a Silent Hill game can be. Turns out, having so many Silent Hill projects developed at the same time was a deliberate strategy set by Konami, and a way to prove to fans that it's serious about the franchise's future.

Speaking to GameSpot at a media roundtable event, Konami producer Motoi Okamoto made it clear that the company views Silent Hill as a major part of its business.
title: Konami Wants You To Know How Serious It Is About Silent Hill

author: Kurt Indovina
description:
Ever since I played three hours of Silent Hill: Townfall and interviewed its writer and director Jon McKellan, one thing McKellan said has been rattling around in my head: "There are different Silent Hills for different people." It's a simple statement--one I agree with and felt silly for not having really considered until playing Silent Hill: Townfall. 

Coming off the heels of Silent Hill f, the biggest departure in the 27-year-old series's formula both in location and gameplay, Townfall carries forward that same trajectory as its predecessor. Silent Hill seems to be entering something of an evolutionary moment, mutating and contorting as it separates itself more and more from the roots of its titular western town. Silent Hill: Townfall is different from other Silent Hills, both mechanically and thematically, in a way that shows this series still has far more to offer beyond its decrepit rusty aesthetics and Bubb
title: Silent Hill: Townfall Could Be Proof Of The Franchise’s Renaissance Moment

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
One way to gauge the success of a game is by looking at how much talk it generates after launch, and in the case of Silent Hill Townfall, game director Jon McKellan has an ambitious goal for the Scottish psychological-horror. According to McKellan, the team at Screen Burn is looking to give players just the right amount of story. By maintaining an air of mystery and ambiguity, it will create a launchpad for people to discuss the themes and plot beats of Silent Hill Townfall for years to come.

"It's a hard--definitely a hard balance--and you won't know until you've released, you know? It's like, we can never unsee what we've seen and unknow what we know, so we think we've struck a balance of never being too explicit, never giving people the true canonical answer, like there's still enough ambiguity
title: Silent Hill: Townfall Dev Wants Players To Discuss Its Story Mysteries For Decades

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Glasgow-based developer Screen Burn has been around for over a decade, and Silent Hill: Townfall is the studio's highest-profile game to date. The studio has produced a few cult-classics over the years like Stories Untold and Observation, but with its Silent Hill spin-off, the team has described being handed the keys to Konami's premier survival-horror franchise as a "confidence builder."

Silent Hill Townfall was announced during Konami's dedicated 2022 livestream for the series, which also saw the announcement of the games Silent Hill f and Bloober Team's Silent Hill 2 remake. According to Silent Hill Townfall game director Jon McKellan, Screen Burn was largely given free rein over the project, with oversight on it being focused on making certain that the game complemented its spooky brethren.
title: Silent Hill: Townfall Devs Were Given The Freedom To Make Their Own Kind Of Horror

author: Richard Li

title: Silent Hill Townfall Hands-On Preview

author: Kurt Indovina
description:
I played three hours of Silent Hill: Townfall, and I'm certain of this: the Silent Hill series is having an evolutionary moment. Coming off the heels of Silent Hill f, the biggest departure from the 27-year-old series's formula both in location and gameplay, Silent Hill: Townfall continues that trajectory, uprooting the series from its titular American town and plopping it in 1990s Scotland. Townfall, like f, is mechanically and thematically different from the franchise's usual tropes, placing an emphasis on its region as the foundation for its horror, rather than that of an individual. It's shaping up to be a well-needed pivot to keep the franchise trudging forward through its own fog.

Silent Hill: Townfall exemplifies Konami's latest strategy in tossing the keys to developers from around the world to carry its flagship horror property, taking a more liberal approach in allowing studios to evolve the series, rather th
title: Silent Hill: Townfall Hands-On Preview
